text:
theo: Heads-up: rolled runtime-3.0.0-beta to canary (na-east) at 15:22Z. Deploybot auto-applied a pinback for model 'summarize-large' after we saw cold-start latency regressions on first-token. Should we keep pinned while we test warmup hooks?

deploybot: Deploy record: runtime-3.0.0-beta -> canary started 2026-05-01T15:22Z. Pin: soft-pin applied automatically for model=summarize-large in cohort=canary. Observability tags: coldstart, batcher. Link: https://deploy.redwood/6290012345 :robot_face:

anika: Paste of metrics: first-token latency median jumped from 18ms -> 62ms on cold containers. Warm containers unaffected. Affected requests ~0.9% of canary traffic (mostly low-traffic customers).

rex: Logs: `batcher: initializing kernel pool on first request, time=41ms` repeated on several pods. Looks like lazy kernel JIT on demand.

ops-sre: Given <1% we can keep soft-pin but propose two mitigations: 1) enable pod warmup hook to run a synthetic init request at startup 2) route sticky traffic for low-qps tenants to runtime-2.19 until warmup confirmed. Suggest routing patch: `if tenant_qps<1 -> runtime-2.19 else runtime-3.0.0-beta` and enable warmup job concurrently. I can stage the route.

theo: Warmup hook sounds good. How long to roll out warmup across canary pods?

ops-sre: Warmup job will run in pod init and cost ~2ms additional CPU; canary rollout in 5-10m. I'll push route change first to reduce impact while warmup propagates.

sam: I'll add a release note under 3.0.0-beta: "Batcher now performs lazy kernel initialization; this may increase first-token latency on cold containers. Mitigation: warmup hooks available; Dedicated customers can opt to pin to runtime-2.19 during migration." Also drafting a short KB for Dedicated admins to enable warmup or pin back.

liz: Any SDK compatibility concerns? sdk-py 1.0.0beta has a warmup header but not required. No tokenization changes. Just operational note.

anika: Quick canary test: enabled warmup on a subset of new pods at 15:33Z; first-token median on warmed pods dropped to 22ms, p95 45ms. Non-warmed pods still ~60ms.

rex: After routing change (tenant_qps<1 -> 2.19) and warmup rollout, affected request fraction fell to 0.12%. Good signal.

ops-sre: Applied routing rule at 15:35Z and wired warmup hook to new canary pods. Added alert: if cold-first-token-rate >1.5% over 5m -> rollback to runtime-2.19 across canary and pause pin.

theo: Plan: 1) keep soft-pin for 1h 2) route low-qps tenants to 2.19 3) enable warmup on all new canary pods 4) monitor cold-start signal and auto-rollback threshold 5) sam publish notes & KB. If stable after 1h, remove pin and proceed with normal rollout.

sam: Release note draft: "runtime-3.0.0-beta introduces dynamic kernel loading for improved throughput; may affect first-token latency on cold instances. Enable warmup hook or temporarily pin to runtime-2.19." Filing docs PR and notifying Dedicated contacts in na-east.

liz: Also added a console banner for affected customers: "If you rely on low-tail first-token latency, consider enabling warmup or pinning to runtime-2.19 while we complete rollout."

ops-sre: Monitoring steady; warmup coverage at 85% of canary pods and cold-start incidents trending down. Keeping auto-rollback hook armed.

rex: Perf artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/perf/6290012345/warmup-test contains traces and flamegraphs showing JIT window.

anika: Closing loop: will watch for 1h window. If no alarms, ops-sre will remove soft-pin and I will post final status here.

theo: Thanks team. If anything spikes, deploybot rollback hook will execute. Posting follow-up in #incidents if we escalate. :rocket:
